questions.q: What does the Latin word 'recreatio', the origin of 'recreation', mean?
questions.explain: Recreation comes from Latin recreatio, 'restoration' of physical and spiritual strength (Topic 1).

questions.q: Which feature always separates tourism from recreation in general?
questions.explain: Recreation can take place at home or in a city park; tourism always involves travel outside the usual environment (Topic 1).

questions.q: An evening walk in a park in your own city is recreation but not tourism.
questions.explain: It restores strength in free time, but there is no travel outside the usual environment (Topic 1).

questions.q: What is the difference between a recreational need and recreational demand?
options: Demand is a need supported by free time and money
A need is always bigger in money terms
questions.explain: Recreational demand is the need backed by free time and money, i.e. a real wish to buy a service (Topic 2).

questions.q: Which of these are functions of recreation described in Topic 2?
questions.explain: The main functions are medical, educational, sports and cultural (plus economic for society); military is not one of them.

questions.q: A school group visits Charyn Canyon to learn about geology. Which function of recreation is strongest here?
questions.explain: Learning new knowledge and impressions is the educational (cognitive) function (Topic 2).

questions.q: Which type of assessment of recreational resources checks slope steepness for skiing or beach width for swimming?
questions.explain: Technological assessment evaluates how suitable a territory is for a certain activity (Topic 3).

questions.q: Historical monuments are classified as which type of recreational resource by renewability?
questions.explain: Historical monuments cannot be restored once destroyed, so they are non-renewable (Topic 3).

questions.q: Which are steps of the point (score) method of assessment?
options: Add points and rank the areas
questions.explain: The point method selects criteria, scores each indicator, adds the points and ranks areas (Topic 3).

questions.q: In CIS practice, drinking mineral water with mineralisation of about 1–10 g/l is called...
questions.explain: Table water is below about 1 g/l, medical-table about 1–10 g/l, medicinal above about 10 g/l (Topic 4).

questions.q: Mineral waters and therapeutic muds are practically inexhaustible resources, so their use does not need to be controlled.
questions.explain: Mineral waters and muds are exhaustible; their use must be controlled and protected (Topics 3–4).

questions.q: Which Kazakhstan resort area is best known for balneological (mineral water) treatment?
questions.explain: Saryagash in Turkestan Region is the best-known mineral-water resort of Kazakhstan (Topics 4–5).

questions.q: Which type of health tourism focuses on prevention and a healthy lifestyle (yoga, fitness, diet) rather than treatment?
options: Medical tourism in the narrow sense
questions.explain: Wellness is a lifestyle approach focused on prevention and balance, not treatment of disease (Topic 5).

questions.q: Which classification criteria are used for recreational tourism in Topic 6?
questions.explain: Recreational tourism is classified by purpose, activity level, duration, season, environment, organisation and participants (Topic 6).

questions.q: Psychological carrying capacity is the limit set by visitor satisfaction: crowding reduces the quality of rest.
questions.explain: Psychological (perceptual) capacity depends on how visitors feel about crowding (Topic 7).

questions.q: At which stage of recreational digression does a forest have bare compacted soil and dying trees?
questions.explain: The fifth (last) stage means the natural complex is destroyed (Topic 7).
